> ## 🧾 2026-08-02 — §0 DEFAULT-OFF FLIP CRITERIA + the standing default audit
>
> **This file is the ONE canonical flags doc.** Do not start a parallel ledger — extend the tables here.
>
> **Standing user directive:** *"don't let me forget about stuff that is default-off that should be on."*
> §0 below is that list: every deliberately default-OFF flag, why it is off, and **what evidence would flip it**.
> A default-OFF flag with no §0 row and no adjudication is a flag nobody has decided about — that is the backlog.
>
> **Two tools keep this file honest — run both before claiming a flag's default:**
> - `node scripts/lint-url-flags.mjs --strict` — reader ↔ docs-row EXISTENCE (undocumented readers, stale rows, off-spellings).
> - `node scripts/audit-flag-defaults.mjs` — reader ↔ docs-cell DEFAULT POLARITY, plus in-code comments that contradict their own reader.
>   `--off` prints the default-OFF docket, `--all` a TSV of every flag, `--mismatch` exits 1 on any finding (CI ratchet).
>

> ## ⚠ 2026-07-23 — the `!== "off"` reader idiom is default-ON BY DESIGN, not a bug pattern to copy
> `nav` (index.html: `botParams.get("nav") !== "off"`) and `netBrain` (`rynth/netbrain.js` `netBrainModeFromUrl`: any value except the literal string `"off"` resolves to `"on"`) both read this way ON PURPOSE — they are intentional default-ON opt-OUTs (rynth-review 14, cross-checked by 02/03/05/07/08/10/13/15/16 against every other flag reader on their surfaces: no other flag was found using this idiom where an opt-IN was intended). **Do not copy this pattern for a new opt-IN flag** — an opt-in reader must be an exact-match check (`=== "1"` / `=== "on"` / truthy-on-a-specific-string), never `!== "off"`, or the flag silently defaults to ON the moment its value is misspelled, absent-but-truthy-checked wrong, or copy-pasted into a context where "off" isn't the only escape string. Every flag below that reads `!== "off"` is intentionally default-on; every flag that reads `=== "<value>"` is an intentional opt-in — if you add a flag, match the one you mean.

> - `missile` (and `attack`/`on`): an aim-level fire is a CYCLE (class 0x40) the links-only
>   swing resolver structurally can't reach; `_tryUnifiedCycleOneShot` builds a one-shot from
>   the cycle bake and animates the full body instead of the single-arm/non-human `setSwingPose`
>   no-op ("missile fires with no animation"). Only diverts when a real cycle resolves.
> - `death` (and `on`): Dead (0x0011) plays the collapse ONCE then HOLDS the final prone
>   frame (one-shot `done`+clamp) — replaces the held-looping pose + racy collapse overlay.
>   The default (flag-off) STATIONARY→cycle path is untouched.
> - `door` (and `on`): door open/close plays the door's real On (`0x4000000b`) / Off
>   (`0x4000000c`) swing via the Rust authority — CYCLE commands the bake resolves, hinge
>   baked into the keyframes (63 of 436 retail MTs carry On/Off cycles; verified by
>   `crates/holtburger-dat/examples/probe_door_motions.rs`). Held as a one-shot at the final
>   frame (`clearOnDone:false`). Replaces the instant root-rotation snap (which spins
>   centred-origin doors in place); §8 Q5 hinge-extraction is NOT needed. The legacy 2D sprite
>   path and the flag-off 3D snap are untouched.
> - `cast` (and `on`): cast gestures (in `MotionTable.links`, like swings) build the same
>   full-body one-shot via `_tryPlayLink` instead of the both-arms-up vibe tween. Covers the
>   server-echo / remote-caster path. Per-SPELL windup variation stays blocked (no
>   `prj_spell_id` on the wire — ACE is kept vanilla), and the deeper local `playCastSequence`
>   (`setTimeout`-paced) replacement is a follow-on; this animates the cast GESTURE, not per-spell.
> - `locomotion` (and `on`): walk/run/idle cycles drive a CYCLIC `MotionSequence` (separate
>   `_unifiedLoco` slot) with gait scaling (anti-ice-skating velScale × server motionSpeed,
>   advancing the playhead faster/slower) + Rust `seekPhase` phase carry across a cycle swap
>   (walk→run no foot-pop). A one-shot (swing/death) suppresses the cycle then resumes it on
>   completion (single playhead). Replaces the mixer `crossFadeTo` + the `CROSSFADE_S=0`/
>   `RESUME_WINDOW` band-aids. The WORKING oracle — migrated LAST; in-world gait UNVERIFIED
>   (no eye-test). Edge cases (true STOP, stance transitions) may need refinement post-eye-test.
>   **NOT in the W6 default** (§9 class-by-class ruling 2026-06-18): locomotion stays behind
>   explicit `?unifiedMotion=locomotion` / `=on` because enabling it by default exposes the
>   open **B-1** movement-integrator overshoot (Walk→Stop→Walk oscillation), which is an
>   upstream `MovementSystem`/`get_state_velocity` bug — fix B-1 first, then fold loco into the default.
> **Logic-verified headlessly** (cargo `motion_sequence` 7/7 parity + one-shot completion + phase;
> `test_motion_sequence.mjs` poser-vs-mixer maxErr 0; `test_motion_sequence_wasm_smoke.mjs`
> drives the real compiled wasm 14/14). **In-world render UNVERIFIED** (no eye-test). Hooks
> (swing swoosh / magic chime / footfall / strike) now FIRE under the flag — drained from the
> bake's hook timeline by the sequence's frame-time through the shared `_fireHooksInRange`
> (Step 6). See `docs/animation-audit/ANIMATION-AUDIT.md` §5.
>

Locked by the Rust test `holtburger_dat::terrain_subdiv::tests::lod_boundary_edges_coincide_across_factors`; `?lodRebake=off` escapes. **CORRECTION (2026-06-28): the Rust physics BSP (`USE_PHYSICS_BSP`/`USE_STATIC_BSP`) is NOT incomplete/off — it is ENABLED + LIVE since 2026-06-16 (commit a7cfb75e), compiled into the shipped wasm.** M1–M4 complete: DAT BSP parse (all node types, faithful to acclient.c + ACE `BSPNode`/`BSPTree`) + broad-phase `sphere_intersects_solid` + narrow-phase `placement_insert_bsp` + integrator hookup (indoor `cell_physics_bsp_solid` solid-gate, outdoor `resolve_static_bsp_pushout`); unit + live-DAT tests pass. ## Remote playtest — quick start (VERIFIED 2026-06-08)

The combined cloudflared quick-tunnel exposes both HTTP and the WebSocket bridge
on one origin (`proxy.cjs:7080` → serve.py:8765 `/*` + wsbridge:8080 `/wsbridge`).

```
https://<tunnel-host>/apps/holtburger-web/?renderer=3d&autoLogin=1&account=tailnet1&password=tailnet1&autoSpawn=first&bridge_url=wss%3A%2F%2F<tunnel-host>%2Fwsbridge&server_host=127.0.0.1&server_port=9000
```

- `<tunnel-host>` = the `*.trycloudflare.com` host of the cloudflared tunnel
  pointed at `:7080`. Find it with:
  `grep -aoE 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com' /proc/<cloudflared-pid>/fd/1`
- `tailnet1` / `tailnet1` is the standing automation account (teleport/Developer privs).
- If a prior session is still in-world, harnesses wait out ACE's session reap between
  boots (s13 inter-arm quiet-gap, `HARNESS_INTER_ARM_GAP_MS`, default 65 s: an abruptly
  closed browser never tells ACE goodbye — wsbridge is WS↔UDP — so ACE holds the session
  until its 60 s network timeout; live-measured s13). `?maxRetries=N` is the opt-in
  stale-session retry.
- Quick-tunnel hosts are **ephemeral** — they rotate whenever cloudflared restarts
  (it has no respawn guard, unlike serve.py/proxy.cjs). Re-grep for the new host.

### ⚠ GOTCHA: `bridge_url` is mandatory for remote, and easy to drop

The login form **defaults to `ws://127.0.0.1:8080/`** (the browser's own loopback),
which never reaches the bridge from a remote device. If you omit `bridge_url` — or
the URL gets **truncated on paste** (messaging apps love to cut at `%` or `&`) — you
get this exact failure cascade:

```
Firefox can't establish a connection to the server at ws://127.0.0.1:8080/.
start_session failed: WsTransport::connect: ws handshake failed
Uncaught Error: closure invoked recursively or after being dropped   ← wasm error-path cascade, NOT a wasm bug
```

The `closure invoked recursively` panic is the wasm's start_session error path
firing on each autoLogin retry — it disappears the moment the handshake succeeds.
Fix = load the **complete** URL including `&bridge_url=wss://<host>/wsbridge`.
(Consider auto-deriving the default bridge from `location.origin` when served over
https, so a bare URL works remotely — see "Possible hardening" at the bottom.)

So while armed, cells.js now moves the **player's-landblock** `buildingsGroup` + `staticsGroup` onto layer 1, making the split read *terrain* vs *everything else* — retail's real division. Chosen over moving TERRAIN to a new layer because layer 1 is already the codebase's "indoor content" layer and is therefore already covered by every light (`lighting.js:276/2466/2642`, `csm.js:245`, `atmosphere_lights.js:174-175`) and every raycaster (`picking.js:476`, `ragdoll_env.js:136-137`); a fresh layer 3 would have unlit terrain and broken terrain picking/ragdoll. Terrain never moves. Blood decals live on `entitiesGroup` (blood_decals.js:862), so the layer-0 restore cannot strand them. **No mask change was needed in atmosphere_pipeline.js.** **NARROWING GRANULARITY.** The baked path offers PER-LANDBLOCK, not per-cell: top-level children carry `userData.landblockId` (buildings.js:490, statics.js:1257, static_batch_x:1758); merged instanced statics carry `coversLbKeys` (statics.js:1444) and may span several LBs. So only the player's own LB is hoisted — other landblocks stay on layer 0, draw in the pre-clear world pass alongside terrain, **keep their terrain occlusion**, and their colour survives the wipe, so the town seen through the doorway is unchanged. `nodeInLandblock` fails CLOSED on an untagged node (stays on layer 0): leaving a node behind means the old bug persists for it — no NEW artifact — whereas hoisting an unknown world-spanning merged batch past the clear would manufacture a fresh see-through. A `BatchedMesh` is one Object3D with one layer mask, and static_atlas.js:1012 comments that the bucket deliberately carries **NO `userData.landblockId`** (that is what keeps the LRU's per-LB scan correct) — so `nodeInLandblock` fails closed on it and it stays on layer 0. **No layer-mask split can isolate one instance out of a shared BatchedMesh.** To exercise the fix on building shells, test with `?indoorDepthSplit=on&statAtlas=off&buildingBatch=off`. > **Stale-entity lifecycle (2026-06-15, always-on, no flag)** — fix for the academy "two leather hats" double-spawn (client-side stale-entity accumulation; ACE serves ONE set, verified on the wire). Two mechanisms: **(1) on ws disconnect (kind=4)**, `entityManager.clearWorldEntities()` drops the dead session's entities so an in-page reconnect/relogin (e.g. the autoLogin kick-dance) re-streams onto an EMPTY map instead of stacking a 2nd set of ACE's freshly-dynamic-guid'd generator items — safe because a reconnect opens a NEW ACE session (fresh per-player ObjMaint → full re-send). **(2) in-session, `entityManager.reapStaleEntities()`** (driven per-frame from the LRU tick in index.js) culls entities whose landblock the player left longer ago than ACE's 25s ObjMaint grace — the retail client contract (ACE keeps the object in its destruction queue 25s and expects the client to cull after, ObjectMaint.cs:41), so ACE re-sends on re-entry. GRACE=30s (>25s) and a wide 8-LB "near" radius mean a portal / PvP dungeon re-entry inside the grace keeps the entity (no invisible opponents). **NOT done via landblock_lru.evict()** — culling on render eviction culls immediately and races the grace. Sites: scene3d/entities.js `clearWorldEntities` + `reapStaleEntities` + scene3d/index.js LRU-tick call + index.html kind-4 arm.

(3) `isTypingInForm` ignores a stale DETACHED `activeElement` (a torn-down panel input can't eat movement keys). Proven by fault injection (one-shot throw on the legacy chat-enable line): flag off → exact State B signature (in-world + gate closed + press edge not forwarded); flag on → keys work, catch counted. `crates/holtburger-core/src/client/movement/system.rs` (top of file). They are
**not** `?query` flags — flipping one means editing the source and **rebuilding
the wasm** (`wasm-pack build …` on the buildbox), then a fresh page load. They
exist for A/B parity work; the **default-off** ones are awaiting a 1070 gait
eye-test before being flipped on. Line numbers drift — grep the const name.

Measured live on the 1070 after a four-town route (`docs/RESULTS-atlas-occupancy-2026-08-05.json`, handoff §11): **29 buckets, 1,941 layers ALLOCATED, 112 layers USED — 551.1 MB allocated against 123 MB occupied**, i.e. **428 MB of nra layers nothing had ever written to**, the single largest item in a 2,445 MB heap on a page that OOM-crashes at ~2,800 MB (`256x256 cap=102 used=14`, `1024x1024 cap=6 used=1`). `_layerCapacityFor` is now only a CEILING: a bucket allocates a handful of layers (4, byte-capped at 2 MiB so a 2048x2048 tile starts at 1 rather than 64 MiB of padding) and DOUBLES, **clamped to that ceiling** — so at no point in a session does a bucket hold more layers than the pre-X7 code allocated on day one. Replayed against the 29 measured buckets: **1,941 → 162 layers, nra 551.1 MB → 131.1 MB (−420 MB), 19 reallocations across the whole route**; the BC7 diffuse twin falls with it (173.8 → 35.0 MB) for **~559 MB total**. Layer depth is fixed by `texStorage3D`, so growth = a NEW array plus a re-upload of the live prefix. Three things make that safe: (1) `makeArrayMaterial`'s `onBeforeCompile` reads the arrays through a mutable HOLDER instead of capturing them, so a RECOMPILE (any program-cache-key change, e.g. light count) cannot resurrect the disposed array, and post-compile swaps re-point `userData._statArrayUniforms` — the same live uniform object `window.__statPom` mutates; (2) every carried-over layer is re-marked with `addLayerUpdate`, which is **required, not an optimisation** — three's first upload of a fresh array runs `texStorage3D` (contents undefined) then uploads ONLY `layerUpdates` (three.module.js:12160-12195 / :12026-12070), so an unmarked carried-over layer is GPU garbage; it is also cheaper than the full-depth upload the empty-set branch would do. (3) BC7 buckets grow too with no `bc7_textures.js` change — a `CompressedArrayTexture` keeps its whole payload in `mipmaps[0].data`, so the blocks are copied from the array's own CPU mirror, nothing re-fetched or retained per layer. Shader source, `customProgramCacheKey`, the geometry/instance path, layer refcounting/recycling and the fail-soft `ptLayerFull` overflow are all untouched; an allocation that is REFUSED leaves the bucket exactly as it was and the prop routes to passthrough. Observe via `__atlasStats()`: `allocLayers` vs `capLayers` (the aggregate the occupancy run wanted), per-bucket `alloc`, and `layerGrows` / `layerGrowUploads` / `layerGrowFails` (the last should stay 0). `=off` allocates at `capacity` again, which also makes the growth path unreachable — a byte-identical escape, not a re-implementation of one. Covered by `test_static_atlas_growth.mjs`. | scene3d/static_atlas.js `statAtlasGrowEnabled` / `_growBucketLayers` |

Sources are only what the singleton path already has — `material.normalMap` (adapter `surfacePixelsToNormalTexture`) with the member's per-category `normalScale` **baked into XY at pack time** (three does `mapN.xy *= normalScale`; baking it keeps `customProgramCacheKey` per-BUCKET, never per-instance), `material.roughness * roughnessMap.g`, and `aoMap.r` at the singleton path's 0.6 intensity. Four `#include` chunks are swapped in `onBeforeCompile` (`map_fragment` also assigns the shared `_statNraTexel`, then `roughnessmap_fragment` / `normal_fragment_maps` / `aomap_fragment`); a 1×1 dummy `normalMap` forces `USE_NORMALMAP_TANGENTSPACE` so three emits the derivative `tbn` frame. Roughness in the B channel is what lets an atlased building pick up the **same T3 sky-IBL env specular the terrain already gets**. Program-cache key gains an `nra` suffix (2 variants → 4, still per-bucket-class). **Memory:** the two arrays SHARE the per-bucket byte budget (`_layerCapacityFor` halves capacity, `_ATLAS_NRA_MAX/MIN_LAYERS` 128/16) — the first cut kept capacity and earlyoom killed the renderer at 5,164 MiB; live working set is 28–59 layers, so the smaller ceiling costs nothing and overflow is fail-soft (`ptLayerFull`). **Not carried:** per-member `metalness` (no free channel; every atlas bucket has always rendered 0 — and 100% of Holtburg statics measured 0.00 anyway) and POM/height. **Validated (SwiftShader, quality=high, Holtburg):** default-flag arm and `=on` arm both boot in-world with **0 console errors**; `=on` links `statAtlasArrayMatV3wnra` across 16 buckets and packs 59/59 layers, **59 with a real normal map**. Flag-ABSENT is proven byte-identical to HEAD (fragment+vertex source, uniform set, cache key, capacity — offline harness against the real r184 `ShaderLib.physical`). **Before a default flip:** a real-GPU 1070 eyetest (batched with the next session) and a look call on the reconstructed-Z vs three's stored-Z normal (terrain's convention, adopted for consistency). `roughnessMap`/`aoMap` currently contribute nothing anywhere — the Phase-5 texchan bake resolves for ~4 DIDs a session, and **neither path has them at Holtburg** — so today the B channel carries the per-material roughness scalar (0.80/0.85/0.90/0.95) instead of the bucket's flat 1.0, and A stays neutral. | scene3d/static_atlas.js:77 |

| `texBc7` | `off` escape | **ON** (flipped 2026-07-30 on the 1070 frame-time A/B; this cell said "off" until 2026-08-02) | `!(off\|0\|false\|no)` + a hard `EXT_texture_compression_bptc` capability gate | **X6 — direct BC7 (BPTC) albedo upload: blocks straight to the GPU, no CPU decode.** Pre-encoded BC7 payloads ride the resource system as namespace `holtburger/tex-bc7`, keyed by **RenderSurface** id (`0x06______`), in an `HBC7` container (`magic "HBC7" | u32 width | u32 height | u32 blocksX | u32 blocksY | 16-B BC7 blocks, row-major`; width/height are TRUE pixel dims and may be non-multiples of 4). The client fetches via the wasm `bc7_blocks(rs_id)` export (empty ⇒ absent, negative-cached), parses/validates in `scene3d/bc7_textures.js`, and uploads as `THREE.CompressedTexture` (singleton materials, swapped in over the RGBA8 twin post-build) or `THREE.CompressedArrayTexture` (statics-atlas buckets, one `compressedTexSubImage3D` per layer via `addLayerUpdate` — strictly cheaper than the RGBA8 arm, which re-uploads the WHOLE array on every layer write). `colorSpace = SRGBColorSpace` makes three pick `COMPRESSED_SRGB_ALPHA_BPTC_UNORM_EXT`, i.e. the same hardware sRGB decode the RGBA8 path gets — **no shader change anywhere**, the atlas's injected `sampler2DArray`/`textureGrad(fract(uv))` chunks and `customProgramCacheKey` are untouched. Atlas bucket keys gain a trailing format field (`f7`/`f8`) because a compressed array's internal format is fixed by `texStorage3D` at allocation and cannot mix with RGBA8 layers; the field is appended ONLY when this flag is live, so a flag-absent key is character-identical to pre-X6. **CAPABILITY-GATED, not just flag-gated:** `initBc7(renderer)` probes `EXT_texture_compression_bptc` on the real context and every consumer reads `bc7Available()`, so a GPU without BPTC (SwiftShader — the dev laptop) behaves exactly like flag-off (without the gate three's `convert()` returns a null gl format and warns per texture). **MIP LEVELS:** `parseHbc7` infers the level count by walking the payload and only enables mipmapped filtering when a chain is actually present — a hard rule, not taste, because `texStorage3D(levels=1)` plus a mipmapped minFilter is an incomplete texture that samples BLACK. No client change was needed for it, as designed. **VRAM:** 8 bpp vs 32 bpp — 4.00x measured across the 2,412-payload corpus (1,152 MiB BC7 vs 4,608 MiB RGBA8). Character is preserved by construction, so there is nothing to sign off on; only resolution and compression fidelity, both measured. **Layers:** terrain codes 0..32 resolve through `src/lib.rs fetch_terrain_textures` (Region `0x13000000` `terrain_desc[].terrain_tex.texture_id` → SurfaceTexture → `highest_res()` → RenderSurface) to just **29 unique RenderSurfaces** — retail shares `0x06006D6F` across BarrenRock/Argila/DesolateLands, `0x06006D4D` across WaterRunning/FauxWaterRunning, `0x06006D3C` across PatchyGrassland/Moss — so the manifest maps layer→rsId and payloads are deduped. **Not the per-rsId shard path:** unlike `?texBc7` (namespace `holtburger/tex-bc7`, keyed by RenderSurface id, for statics), terrain builds ONE array texture, so this is the ATLAS BUILDER consuming BC7 into a `THREE.CompressedArrayTexture` — easier than statics, because a compressed array needs one fixed (format, w, h) for every layer and terrain layers already share dimensions. **MIPS, unlike `?texBc7` v1:** every payload is HBC7 **v2** (same 20-byte header, full halving chain appended to 1x1 — `parseHbc7` infers the count), box-downsampled from the SOURCE pixels and encoded per level, never by re-encoding decoded BC7. That is what makes `LinearMipmapLinearFilter` + full anisotropy legal here; terrain is the most tiling, most distance-viewed surface in the game and level-0-only would shimmer badly — and `texStorage3D(levels=1)` with a mipmapped minFilter is an INCOMPLETE texture that samples BLACK. **nra is DERIVED from the retail albedo, not carried over from CC0** (Sobel-from-luminance normal, luminance roughness, concavity AO, luminance height→alpha for T4 POM). Pairing CC0 `nra` with a retail albedo is not merely a style mismatch: the POM march reads *height* and offsets `cellUv` before every sample, so a foreign heightfield makes relief slide against the visible texels. Water layers 16-20/22 are NOT derived — they keep the flat `(128,128,230,255)` texel because the terrainplan §4 water shader owns them. **Mutually exclusive with `?pbrTerrain`** (both write the same layers' albedo); when this flag wins, the CC0 load is skipped and `pbrTerrainState` is fed the derived BC7 nra array. **VRAM:** t1024 (default) = 88.0 MiB for both arrays (44.0 each) — **EXACTLY VRAM-NEUTRAL** against the 88.0 MiB RGBA8 arm it replaces, at **2x the linear resolution** and 11 mip levels; t512 = 22.0 MiB (**4.0x saving** at retail-native resolution, 10 mip levels). Wire cost is the real trade: 81 MB vs 20 MB first visit (~15 min vs ~4 min at 666 kbps) — pin `512` on a constrained line. 2048 is deliberately not a tier — 352 MiB. **CAPABILITY-GATED** on `EXT_texture_compression_bptc` via the shared `bc7Available()`, so a no-BPTC GPU behaves exactly like flag-off. Needs the gitignored `scene3d/assets/terrain_bc7/<tier>/` bake; absent manifest → one console warn + today's render. Diag: `window.__terrainBc7Stats()`. **1070 LOOK-PASS QUEUED (not waived):** default flipped ON 2026-08-04 by user direction after a bare-default SwiftShader validation (loads+spawns+0 errors); the aesthetic items — derived normal green-channel sign, derived-height POM, retail-vs-CC0 look — still need real motion on real hardware and sit in the vistest queue. `?terrainBc7=off` A/Bs back to the CC0 arm. Measured live at `mid`: both t1024 arrays shipped `anisotropy: 4` on a GPU reporting 16, and at 4 taps a 1024² atlas resolves to about what a 512² one does on a receding ground plane — i.e. the entire t1024 tier was being filtered away before it reached the screen. ## Possible hardening (not yet implemented)

The remote-bridge failure above is a footgun: omit `bridge_url` and it silently
falls back to localhost. A robust default would be, in the `bridge_url` prefill
(index.html ~7612): when no param is given **and** the page is served over
`https:` on a non-loopback host, default the form to
`` `wss://${location.host}/wsbridge` `` (and `server_host`/`server_port` likewise
when behind the combined proxy). Then a bare remote URL "just works" and only
explicit overrides need the param. Low-risk; takes effect on next page load (the
service worker does not cache `index.html`).

### 2026-06-23 — ambient swarm fidelity: Swarm trajectory + static CallPES loop (JS-only)

Root-caused from the retail decomp (`acclient.c`) cross-checked against ACE.Server + Chorizite + real `client_portal.dat` bytes: ambient butterflies/insects are **scenery** with a `default_script` (0x33) that does `CreateParticle(Swarm 0x32…) + CallPES(self)`. Two client deviations kept them from "flying around": (1) the Swarm trajectory math was ported wrong, and (2) the static walker dropped the `CallPES` re-play loop, so finite swarms (e.g. `0x320002b5`, total=60) burst once at LB-load and never returned. ### 2026-07-27 — COL-20 remote turn-phase animation gate (JS-only, F4)

| Flag | What it does | Eye-test | Pass criteria |
|------|--------------|----------|---------------|
| **`?remoteTurnGate=off`** | Escape hatch. DEFAULT ON. A `MoveToObject`/`MoveToPosition` envelope reaches remote rigs as a bare forward-locomotion hint (`moveto_locomotion_hint`, lib.rs:6710) with no facing information, so a chased creature used to start its RUN cycle the instant the chase was ordered — while still rotating ("over eager to run before completely facing"). Retail cannot do that: the MoveTo pending queue is `[TurnToHeading, MoveToPosition]` and `BeginTurnToHeading` plays the turn-in-place cycle until the turn node is consumed (acclient.c:345456-345518/:345859). With no remote MoveToManager to sequence nodes, the gate uses retail's own while-moving aux-turn tolerance — 20.0 degrees (`HandleMoveToPosition` :345636) — as the switch point. Bounded by a 3.5 s valve so a stale heading target can never pin a creature in its turn/rest pose. | Walk past an aggro mob so it 180 degree re-targets you; watch the clip it plays while rotating | Default: turn-in-place cycle plays through the sweep, run/walk starts as the facing lands (zero run-cycle frames while the error exceeds 90 degrees); `=off`: the eager run cycle returns. Position/travel identical either way. |

### Far terrain — retail range fog + the Far Composite Ring **[far-terrain wave, 2026-08-03]**

The horizon problem is **~70 % absent content and ~30 % shading**. Content stopped at 1056 m
(axis) while the DAT has real land out past 1500 m, so the top 39–49 % of every long sightline
was backstop, not Dereth. Retail closed the same view with **authored linear range fog**
(`SkyDesc::GetWorldFog`, acclient.c:301602 — Dereth clear day `min 150 → max 2400`,
`0xFFC3C8DC`, lerped per `SkyTimeOfDay`) over a **radius-8 (1536 m)** default landblock grid.
This wave ships both halves: the fog (`terrainFog`, ON) and the extra content (`farRing`).

Reader for all of these: `scene3d/far_terrain_flags.js`. Effect sites: `scene3d/far_terrain.js`,
`scene3d/terrain_shared_glsl.js`, `scene3d/terrain.js` (tail), `scene3d/loop.js`.

| Flag | Reader (semantics when absent) | Effective default | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `farTerrain` | `off\|0\|false\|no` disables; anything else ON | **ON** — master escape for the whole wave (fog **and** ring). `?farTerrain=off` restores the pre-wave client: no terrain fog, no far ring, `fogLerp` back to opt-in. **⚠ `?farTerrain=off` does NOT restore the aerial wash.** `horizonFade`/`aerialDepth` and their `AERIAL_MAX`/`AERIAL_DESAT` constants were retired *independently* of this wave's flags (see the adjudication block below), so `?farTerrain=off` alone gives you a client with **neither** the fog **nor** the wash. The full pre-wave arm is `?farTerrain=off&aerialDepth=on&aerialMax=0.62&aerialDesat=0.72`. | far_terrain_flags.js `farTerrainEnabled` |
| `terrainFog` | `off\|…` disables (AND-ed with `farTerrain`) | **ON** — **S1.** Puts retail range fog in the terrain fragment shader. The terrain `ShaderMaterial` previously contained the token `fog` exactly twice, both on the *wireframe* `MeshBasicMaterial`s — `scene.fog` had **never** affected the ground, which is why nobody could close the horizon with it. Terrain now sets `fog: true` + three's own `fogColor/fogNear/fogFar` uniforms and runs three's `<fog_fragment>` arithmetic verbatim (hand-written: the shader is GLSL3 with a custom `out`), so terrain, statics and models fog **identically** at a shared silhouette edge. Plane-based like three, **not** retail's `D3DRS_RANGEFOGENABLE` radial — matching three matters more than matching retail here, because a terrain/statics disagreement is visible and a corner-of-screen radial difference is not. OFF ⇒ `USE_FOG` is never defined and the fragment shader is byte-identical to the pre-wave build. | far_terrain_flags.js `terrainFogEnabled`; terrain_shared_glsl.js `TERRAIN_FOG_TAIL_GLSL` |
| `fogLerp` | `on\|1\|true\|yes` forces ON, `off\|0\|false\|no` forces OFF, **absent ⇒ `terrainFog`** | **ON** (was `=== "on"` opt-in). Retail's authored 2400 m sat against a 1536 m grid, so its edge was at ~62 % fog and never seen; our terrain edge is a *streaming* limit that moves (near ring 5, far ring `farRadius`, and the geometry governor has been measured collapsing the near ring 200 → 35 LBs), so the authored value alone would leave a hard unfogged cut. With the clamp, an absent / unbaked / off-map tile is **invisible** and the "void read as ocean" mis-tune cannot recur. **⚠ `R_effective` counts LB CENTRES**, and a landblock is 192 m wide, so the outermost DRAWN edge is `(R + 0.5) × 192` — the old `0.85 × R × 192` clamped ~0.77 of the real edge and measured 816 m at R = 5, putting the whole visible world inside the ramp (mid-valley terrain at 400 m read 201/255 vs 134/255 with the authored 2400 m band). | far_terrain_flags.js `farFogFrac`; far_terrain.js `farTerrainEffectiveRadiusLb` |

Measured after: fogged-terrain-vs-sky delta **≤ 9.6/255 at 09:00 and 19:00, ≤ 1.1/255 at 02:00** (was 21–25 and 15–19). `=off` restores the authored hex. | far_terrain_flags.js `farFogSkyProbeEnabled`; loop.js `sampleHorizonSkyRadiance` |

HD520 during a fill: 9 near LBs resident and **zero** patches baked reported `r = 8` → fogFar
1305 m with drawn terrain ending at 288 m, i.e. the fog stopped hiding the true edge for the
whole fill. It is now the larger of (a) the near ring's measured radius, unfloored, and
(b) `farRingSolidRadiusLb` — the largest Chebyshev radius whose landblocks are **all** covered
by a far patch that is baked AND in the scene graph, open-smoothed at 0.05 LB/step and dropping
to reality instantly so it can never exceed what is drawn. The re-validator's check is
`fog.far <= fog.drawnEdgeM` at **every** sample of a fresh boot; measured across a full fill,
`273.6/288.0 → 364.8/384.0 → … → 1003.2/1056.0`, no violation, including the pre-in-world phase
(where the clamp used to leave the `THREE.Fog` constructor's seeded 2500 m in place because
`far < near` silently skipped the write).

> 1. **The dissolve cannot reach the band it exists for.** `HorizonDissolveEffect` opens with `depth >= 0.9999 → passthrough`.
>    With the live `near 0.1 / far 5000` that is a hard cutoff at **833.4 m** (measured 831–901 m). **96 % of the shipped
>    820→1150 m band was inside the dead zone**; dissolve-only vs off whole-frame MAD measured 0.56–2.04, i.e. noise.
>    Deriving a *wider* band from a bigger ring radius puts **100 %** of it in the dead zone — strictly worse.
> 2. **The aerial wash's strength is inverted with distance.** Per-row MAD on/off at four vantages: **0.00–2.46** on the
>    farthest terrain rows vs **15.7–27.7** on the mid-field. It greyed the mid-ground while the horizon kept full chroma —
>    the opposite of aerial perspective. It also desaturated *water* as hard as land (the Holtburg river went cyan → murky).
> 3. **It was tuned against a backstop.** Past ~1056 m there was no geometry at all; the "ocean" was the takram sky's dark
>    planet **ground** showing through absent landblocks. The oracle says the DAT has dry land at heights 43–99 m out to
>    1500 m+. Never tune a distance treatment against a frame whose distance is absent content.
>
> **The replacement is `terrainFog` below** — retail's own authored linear range fog, in world space, with real depth,
> monotone in distance by construction, reaching the full far plane. Restore the old look for an A/B with
> `?aerialDepth=on&aerialMax=0.62&aerialDesat=0.72`. The `?aerialDebug` harness still builds the pass (and was rewritten
> on 2026-08-03 into a binary depth-sanity read with a calibration wedge — see its row above).
>
> **⚠ The retirement is INDEPENDENT of `?farTerrain`.** Turning the far-terrain wave off does **not** bring the wash back,
> because `AERIAL_MAX` and `AERIAL_DESAT` are now `0.0` in the source and `horizonFadeEnabled` defaults to `false`
> regardless of any far-terrain flag. A "before this wave" arm therefore needs **both** halves:
> `?farTerrain=off&aerialDepth=on&aerialMax=0.62&aerialDesat=0.72`. `?farTerrain=off` on its own gives a client with
> neither the fog nor the wash, which is not the pre-wave look and must not be compared against as if it were.
